letter.title: A letter of gratitude
lines: Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, to our dear newlyweds.
Today the whole GMSA-KNUST family lifts its hands and its hearts for you.
Thank you for the time, the effort and the sincerity you gave to this association. We saw it, and Allah sees it, and it is never forgotten.
Whatever you gave quietly, may it be written for you as a gift that keeps giving.
Hearts once apart, now closely aligned. What a beautiful way to begin.
May Allah bless what He has brought together, and make your home a place of tranquillity, affection and mercy.
letter.signature: With love and gratitude, the GMSA-KNUST family

DUMMY: May Allah make your home a place of calm and love.
DUMMY: Thank you for the memories. Happy marriage!
DUMMY: May every day together be better than the last.
DUMMY: Your service inspired many of us. Barakallahu feekuma.
DUMMY: Wishing you patience, laughter and lasting happiness.

names.lead: May this be the beginning of a blessed life together
names.verseArabic: وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنْ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَزْوَاجًا لِّتَسْكُنُوا إِلَيْهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيْنَكُم مَّوَدَّةً وَرَحْمَةً ۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَآيَاتٍ لِّقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
names.verseTranslation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquillity in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
names.duaArabic: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكُمَا وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكُمَا وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِي خَيْرٍ
names.duaTransliteration: Barakallahu lakuma wa baraka alaykuma wa jama'a baynakuma fi khayr
names.duaTranslation: May Allah bless you both, send His blessings upon you, and bring you together in goodness.
names._verifyNote: Display the Arabic strings exactly as given. Do not edit or re-type Arabic. The narrated wording uses the singular (laka, alayka); the dual form is the common adaptation for a couple. Add this note to README for the imam to confirm before sending.
